title: 晨钟暮鼓: Xi'an Ran on a Bell and a Drum for 600 Years | China Travel Expert
description:
Before clocks, Xi'an kept time with two buildings. The idiom is 晨钟暮鼓 — "morning bell, evening drum." A great bell in the Bell Tower rang at dawn to open the city gates; a drum in the Drum Tower, a few hundred metres west, beat at dusk to close them.

The Bell Tower you see today was built in 1384 under the first Ming emperor and sits almost dead-center of Xi'an's old walled city (it was moved to that exact spot in 1582 as the city grew). The Drum Tower is slightly older, from 1380. Together they're one of the best-preserved bell-and-drum pairs in China — and for centuries they were the city's alarm clock, its gate schedule, and its emergency siren all in one.

🧭 Expert Tip: come at dusk. Both towers are floodlit after dark and sit on a traffic island you circle underground — the night view beats the daytime one.

钟楼建于1384年，位于西安老城正中；晨钟暮鼓，钟楼早晨鸣钟开城门，鼓楼傍晚击鼓闭城门。
